summary: JIT elevation issues: temporary session issued but missing RBAC claims, immediate 403 on console routes
summary_extended: Users complete Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation flow via Okta but the resulting session token lacks role claims required for console access; requests to per-route admin APIs return 403 immediately after elevation.
description:
Issue summary:
- Several engineers reported being able to complete the Okta JIT MFA + approver flow, receive a console session, but then immediately get 403 on routes that require elevated roles.

Impact:
- Affected users can temporarily elevate but cannot perform elevated tasks (deploys, infra access) for the duration of the elevated window.
- First reported for 3 users in production US-WEST; could affect others using JIT in the same tenant.

Environment:
- Prod (us-west cluster)
- Okta tenant: redwood-production.okta.com
- Console version: 2.9.1
- JIT flow uses Okta inline hook to transform role claims and issue short-lived elevation grant via SSO token.

Steps to reproduce:
1) User without elevated roles clicks "Request elevation" in Console.
2) Okta prompts for MFA and notifies approver in #approvals slack channel.
3) Approver accepts via Slack approval link.
4) User receives a console session and redirect to /console/dashboard.
5) Immediately attempt action requiring elevated role (e.g., POST /api/v1/deploy or access /admin/audit).

Observed behavior:
- Console responds with HTTP 403 and body: "missing required role claim: admin:deploy".
- Session token in browser lacks the expected roles array (claims truncated).
- Okta system logs show the inline hook executed but returned a payload with roles joined as a single truncated string (length ~800 chars).

Expected behavior:
- Elevated session token should include full roles array (admin:deploy, admin:rollouts, etc.) and elevated actions should succeed.

Temporary workaround:
- Re-authenticating via Okta SSO (full sign-out and sign-in) returns a session with correct claims for some users.
- Manual grant of role via admin console fixes access until token expiry.

Attachments/links:
- Related Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0ABC1234/p1678480000000
- Okta system log excerpt: https://okta.redwood.com/logs/evt-98432
steps_to_reproduce: Complete Okta MFA and have approver accept via Slack link
Attempt elevated API call and observe 403
observed_logs: Console API: 403 missing required role claim: admin:deploy
comments: Aisha Patel (reporter) 2026-03-10: Initial report from oncall — 3 engineers unable to perform elevated deploys after JIT success.

Marcus Chen (assignee) 2026-03-11: Reproduced with test user; confirmed roles claim present as a single long string rather than JSON array. Suspect Okta inline hook serialization or HTTP header size truncation between Okta and our auth service.

SRE (L. Gomez) 2026-03-11: Checked ingress logs — no 413s or header truncation at edge LB. Payload size looks below standard thresholds. Suggest checking the inline hook implementation and any escaping changes introduced in 2026-03-08 hook update.

Identity (R. Singh) 2026-03-12: Found that a recent change in the inline-hook library switched from returning JSON array to CSV-joined string when roles>5. Rolling back to previous hook helper for testing.
Marcus Chen 2026-03-12: Running canary with reverted hook helper for tenant redwood-production; requesting verification from affected users.
investigation_notes: Confirmed reproducer: when hook returns roles as CSV string, our tokenization code expects array and ends up storing one string which our RBAC check doesn't parse => 403.
The inline-hook library was updated on 2026-03-08 (PR #4321) to optimize payloads; regression introduced for multi-value claims formatting.
Edge LB and auth proxy do not truncate cookie or header sizes for this tenant; no infrastructure-level 413 observed.
Risk assessment: medium — affects only JIT flows that result in >5 roles assigned (relatively uncommon but present for platform admins).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 Marcus Chen: Rolled back inline-hook helper to pre-2026-03-08 behavior for redwood-production tenant. Verified affected users can now elevate and access admin routes without 403.
Deployed hotfix to identity service to accept CSV-joined roles temporarily and parse into arrays to tolerate both formats (short-term mitigation).
Follow-up: schedule stable fix to inline-hook library to always return JSON arrays and add unit tests for multi-role claims (assigned to Identity team, due 2026-03-20).
resolution: Partial fix deployed; rollback of hook plus tolerant parsing applied; stable library fix planned.
status_summary: In Progress — mitigation applied and affected users validated; permanent library patch in progress.
